summary.text: Scott Fluhr is the Republican candidate for the Indiana House of Representatives, District 70, in the November 3, 2026 general election; he won the Republican primary on May 5, 2026 over John Colburn.
According to his campaign website, he is a human resources analyst and has chaired the Harrison County Republican Party for over eighteen years.

paragraphs.text: Scott Fluhr describes himself on his campaign website as a lifelong Harrison County resident from Corydon, and says he went to St. Joseph Catholic School and Corydon Central High School and graduated from Indiana University Bloomington with a business degree.

The site says he volunteers as chairman of the Harrison County Popcorn Festival Parade, president of the Harrison County Parks & Recreation Board, and a member of the Harrison County Tourism Board, and that he belongs to the Knights of Columbus and the National Rifle Association.

His campaign website lists endorsements from Indiana Right to Life, the National Rifle Association Political Victory Fund, the Indiana State Fraternal Order of Police, the National Federation of Independent Business Indiana PAC, and the Indiana Manufacturers Association, among others.
The site says he wants to send "conservative voices" to Indianapolis to defend "faith, family, freedom, and hard work."
